co_pulpit_rock.blurb: Pulpit Rock is a broad granite buttress in Cow Creek Canyon, in the Estes Park valley, set in wilderness country at roughly 7,600 feet. Much of the face lies back well short of vertical, so the climbing is friendly slab and crack work rather than steep sustained pitching. Seventeen routes are mostly gear-protected, with a handful of top-rope lines. Most sit around the 5.8 level, with a few easier and a few harder up to low 5.11. Cracks tend to peter out, so expect to place gear in short stretches. Multi-pitch lines of several hundred feet offer views over the valley. It suits climbers who like moderate traditional routes close to the road.

co_box_the.blurb: The Box is a Flatiron high on Dinosaur Mountain above Boulder, reached by hiking the switchbacks between it and the Finger Flatiron. It has climbing on both its north and south sides. The sport lines are the draw: mostly 5.11 through 5.13, steep and demanding, on the south Scoop Wall and the north face. Gear routes run from very easy up to 5.10, including a two-pitch crack climb that splits the formation, and the descent crosses over the top through a notch. There is one boulder problem too. Seventeen climbs in total make it a small, focused venue best suited to strong sport climbers and confident trad leaders.

co_prow_the_2.blurb: The Prow is a sport crag in the Lime Park canyon near Eagle, at about 9,200 feet, so it stays cool in summer. Seventeen bolted routes span a wide range: a cluster of easy-to-moderate lines around 5.8 and 5.9, a good number of 5.10s, and a smaller group of 5.11 to low 5.13 test pieces. Several routes at the easier end are popular warm-ups for newer leaders. The wall can see crowds in peak season. Reaching it means parking at the end of the west-side road, crossing the creek on a makeshift footbridge and following a climbers trail uphill to the left fork under the prow.
